newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Arrest warrant sought for South Korean banker.
newsitem.headline: Arrest warrant sought for South Korean banker.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Friday they were seeking an arrest warrant for the president of SEOULBANK in connection with a bribery scandal.
"We filed a request with the court for an arrest warrant for SEOULBANK president Sohn Hong-gyun tonight on bribery allegations," a prosecution official said.

Prosecutors summoned Sohn earlier today to question him on allegations that he had taken tens of millions of won (tens of thousands of dollars) from two to three companies for providing illegal loans.
Prosecution officials refused to give further details.
SEOULBANK spokesman Lee Jae-yong confirmed the bank's president was now under investigation by prosecutors but declined to comment further.
In August, Rhee Chul-soo, former president of Korea First Bank, was sentenced to three years in jail for bribery.
Rhee was found guilty of accepting 280 million won in return for approving millions of dollars worth of loans to two local companies.
